transcript: Flipping your class? You don't need a studio. The lecture slides you already have can become short pre-class videos your students will actually watch.
Your slides are already sequenced and matched to your learning outcomes. As videos, students can pause and rewatch, read captions, and hear the same explanation every time.
Plan short videos, not recorded lectures. A week on supply and demand becomes four short videos, one concept each, and each one names what students will do in class.
Trim each slide to the key idea and move explanations into your notes. Those notes become the narration, so write them for the ear, and end with a link to class.
Put each video in Moodle, Canvas or Blackboard, right beside the activity that depends on it. And tell students the viewing time up front: twelve minutes of video before Tuesday.

Start with one week and make two or three short videos. Try Basic first, or let Pro's a.i. direct your deck into a produced explainer. Ordinary slides in, extraordinary video out at powerpoint2vid.com.
